flawed_step: Step 1 of the proof: turning the closed Euler trail, which uses every edge, into a cycle through every vertex by skipping repeated vertices. Skipping a repeated vertex needs an edge between the vertices on either side of it, and that edge may not exist. Neither being 2-connected nor having all even degrees supplies such edges, so this step cannot be justified.
counterexample: K_{2,4}, the complete bipartite graph with parts {a1,a2} and {b1,b2,b3,b4}. The a-vertices have degree 4 and the b-vertices have degree 2, all even, and the graph is connected, so it is Eulerian. It is 2-connected: it has 6 vertices, deleting an a-vertex leaves the star K_{1,4}, and deleting a b-vertex leaves K_{2,3}; both are connected. It is not Hamiltonian: a cycle in a bipartite graph alternates between the two parts, so a cycle through all 6 vertices would need both parts to be the same size, but here they have sizes 2 and 4.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The natural proof tries to shortcut an Euler circuit into a Hamiltonian cycle, and that step fails. K_{2,4} is 2-connected and Eulerian, but it is not Hamiltonian because it is bipartite with parts of unequal size.
